title: Phage Stock Preparation
author: Marijn Ceelen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7kthkwn
materials: Determine phage titer using plaque or spot assay.

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Host
steps.instruction: Grow E. coli bacterial host (e.g., LE392, DH10B, or DH5alpha) in LB medium overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Salt Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare and autoclave 1 M CaCl2 and 1 M MgCl2.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 1 M CaCl2 and 50 µL of 1 M MgCl2 to 50 mL of LB medium.
Inoculate each aliquot with 0.1 volumes of the overnight bacterial host.

steps.title: Incubate Bacterial Culture
steps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated culture at 37 °C with agitation for 1 hour.

steps.title: Infect with Phage
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of high titer phage lysate (> 10^8 PFU/ml) to the culture.

steps.title: Incubate for Lysis
steps.instruction: Incubate at 37 °C with agitation for approximately 5 hours or until the lysate clears.

steps.title: Collect and Store Lysate
steps.instruction: Collect the phage lysate and store at 4 °C until clean up.

steps.title: Centrifuge Phage Lysate
steps.instruction: Pool phage lysate into 50 mL sterile falcon centrifuge tubes and centrifuge at 4,000 rpm for 25 minutes.

steps.title: Filter-Sterilize Supernatant
steps.instruction: Filter-sterilize the phage supernatant using a 0.22 μm filter to obtain a bacterial cell-free phage lysate.
